Nesta learns what the healers have told Rhysand and what he has chosen to keep from his wife: the child has its father's wings, Feyre's body was not made to bear it, and as things stand the birth will kill her. Nesta is left holding a secret that is not hers, in a family that has never trusted her with anything.

Nesta breaks the secret open. In front of the family she tells Feyre what Rhysand has been hiding about the pregnancy, and the room turns on her; being right does not excuse the way she did it. She is sent out of Velaris to the Illyrian mountains in disgrace, and everything she had built - the training, the library, her friends, the House itself - is cut away at once. At the same time the court moves against Briallyn and Koschei: Cassian and Azriel are caught in an ambush where the Crown is used against them and come very close to dying. Isolated in a war camp with Emerie for company, Nesta has to face what she did and what she wants to be instead, while the Illyrians around her make plain how little a female is welcome there.

Nesta, Emerie and Gwyn are swept into the Blood Rite, the Illyrians' annual trial: hundreds of warriors stripped of weapons, magic and the use of their wings and turned loose in the mountains to fight their way to the sacred peak of Ramiel over a week. No female has ever been permitted in it. The three keep together, are hunted for the offence of being there, and fight through Illyrians who mean to kill them. When the alternative is losing her friends, Nesta uses the Mask and raises the dead to fight beside her, and pays for it afterward. The three of them reach the mountain and Nesta touches the stone at its summit, winning the Rite outright - a result the Illyrians can neither dismiss nor undo.

Nesta comes down from the mountain to find Feyre in labour and dying exactly as the healers predicted. She bargains away the power she took from the Cauldron in exchange for her sister's life, remaking Feyre's body so that the birth can happen. Feyre survives and her son Nyx is born. Nesta comes out of it stripped of most of what the Cauldron gave her, reconciled with Feyre for the first time since they were mortal, and finally done punishing herself for their father's death; what she keeps is what she built instead - the training, the library, and the two friends who went into the mountains with her. She and Cassian acknowledge the mating bond between them and stop fighting it. Briallyn is killed and the immediate danger from the Dread Trove passes, but Koschei is untouched at his lake and still holds the queen Vassa, Eris's arrangements with the Night Court are unresolved, Elain's situation is unchanged, and the Illyrians must now live with three women who won the Blood Rite.

characters.description: The narrator, a nineteen-year-old huntress who keeps her impoverished family fed by poaching in the frozen woods near a mortal village, south of the wall that separates the human lands from the faerie realm of Prythian. Hardened, illiterate, and fiercely practical, she resents and fears the faeries her people were taught to hate. Self-taught at survival and quietly in love with color and painting, she carries a childhood promise to her dying mother to look after the family that rarely thanks her. When she kills a wolf in the snow that proves to be a disguised faerie, she sets in motion everything that follows.
characters.name: Feyre Archeron

characters.description: Feyre's eldest sister, proud, sharp-tongued, and cold. Bitter over the poverty into which their once-wealthy family has fallen, she refuses menial work and clashes constantly with Feyre. Beneath the hardness lies a fierce, stubborn will and a refusal to bow to anyone.
characters.name: Nesta Archeron

characters.description: Feyre's gentle middle sister, soft-spoken and kind, who loves her garden and dreams of an ordinary, comfortable life. Warmer than Nesta but just as unsuited to hardship, she offers Feyre quiet affection amid the family's decline.
characters.name: Elain Archeron

characters.description: A powerful faerie who comes to the family's cottage in the shape of an enormous beast to demand a life in payment for the wolf Feyre killed, then takes her across the wall instead of killing her. He is the High Lord of the Spring Court, one of the rulers of Prythian, able to shift between a man's form and a monstrous one. Golden-haired and green-eyed, he wears a jeweled mask he cannot remove, a sign of a blight troubling his lands. Gruff and guarded at first, he proves unexpectedly gentle, giving Feyre freedom of his estate rather than treating her as a captive.
characters.name: Tamlin

characters.description: A red-haired faerie of the Spring Court with a mechanical golden eye, Tamlin's close friend and emissary. Quick with a barbed remark and openly contemptuous of Feyre as a mortal intruder at first, he thaws toward her over time. He carries old scars and a hard past from another court, along with a wary loyalty to Tamlin.
characters.name: Lucien

characters.description: A faerie servant in Tamlin's household who looks after Feyre. Brisk and cautious, she gradually softens, warning Feyre about the court's dangers and slowly revealing pieces of the history and curse that Tamlin refuses to discuss.
characters.name: Alis

characters.description: The High Lord of the Night Court, reputed to be the most powerful and most feared ruler in Prythian. He first appears at a Spring Court festival, catching Feyre where she should not be and unsettling her with his beauty, cruelty, and casual menace. Dangerous and unreadable, he seems to serve hidden purposes of his own.
characters.name: Rhysand

characters.description: The self-styled queen who rules from Under the Mountain, having seized control over the High Lords of Prythian and spread the blight afflicting their courts. Cruel, vain, and immensely powerful, she keeps the seven High Lords in thrall and delights in others' suffering. She is the source of the curse laid on Tamlin and the Spring Court.
characters.name: Amarantha

recaps.ending: Feyre completes Amarantha's final trial only by stabbing three faeries through the heart; the first two are innocents, and the third is Tamlin himself, whose heart Amarantha has turned to stone so the blade cannot kill him. Even so, Amarantha refuses to free the courts because Feyre never solved her riddle. Feyre says the answer aloud - love - and Amarantha, enraged, breaks her neck and kills her. The seven High Lords, including Rhysand, each pour a shard of their own power into her, resurrecting her as an immortal High Fae. Freed, Tamlin kills Amarantha, and the courts are released from her rule and the blight. Feyre returns to the Spring Court reborn and reunited with Tamlin, but haunted by the innocents she killed and changed forever by her new nature. She also carries the bargain Rhysand struck with her Under the Mountain: one week of every month is now owed to the Night Court, a debt that will shape what comes next.
recaps.in_short: Nineteen-year-old huntress Feyre kills a wolf in the winter woods that turns out to be a faerie, and a great beast comes to claim a life in return, taking her across the wall into Prythian. The beast is Tamlin, High Lord of the Spring Court, cursed to wear a mask while a blight ravages the faerie lands. Living on his estate, Feyre falls in love with him, but he sends her home to keep her safe from a growing danger. Learning that Tamlin has been dragged Under the Mountain by the tyrant queen Amarantha, Feyre returns to save him. Amarantha forces her through three deadly trials or a riddle to win his freedom; the mysterious Rhysand, High Lord of the Night Court, aids her at a price, binding her to spend part of each month in his court. Feyre survives the trials but is killed by Amarantha, only to be resurrected as an immortal High Fae by the seven High Lords. Amarantha is destroyed, the courts are freed, and Feyre returns to the Spring Court remade, carrying deep trauma and her bargain with Rhysand.

recaps.text: Feyre Archeron supports her impoverished family by hunting in the woods near a mortal village. When she kills a large wolf that proves to be a disguised faerie, a monstrous beast comes to her family's cottage and demands a life in payment under an ancient treaty. Rather than kill her, the beast takes Feyre across the wall into Prythian, the faerie realm her people fear. There the beast reveals himself as Tamlin, High Lord of the Spring Court, who can shift between man and monster and wears a jeweled mask he cannot remove. His friend and emissary Lucien treats Feyre coldly at first. Given the run of a beautiful estate rather than imprisoned, Feyre slowly realizes that something is deeply wrong in these lands - a blight is spreading, faeries are disappearing, and her hosts speak of a threat they will not name.

Living among the faeries, Feyre begins to lower her guard. She learns fragments of the court's troubles from the servant Alis and grows closer to Tamlin, who is gentler and more burdened than she expected. She witnesses the danger of the faerie world firsthand and comes to understand that the blight afflicting Prythian is tied to some larger menace pressing on the Spring Court. At a wild festival tied to the land's magic, the cruel and beautiful Rhysand, High Lord of the Night Court, discovers Feyre where she should not be. He unnerves her with his menace even as he spares her, hinting that powerful forces beyond Tamlin's control are closing in on them all.

Feyre and Tamlin fall in love, and for a while the estate becomes a refuge of painting, quiet, and stolen happiness. But Tamlin grows increasingly troubled, and the pressure on the Spring Court mounts. Feyre pieces together hints of a curse and a looming reckoning, sensing that the danger is far worse than anyone will tell her. Tamlin, desperate to protect her from what is coming, makes the wrenching decision to send Feyre back across the wall to her human family, ending their idyll to keep her out of the enemy's reach.

Back among her family, who have risen in fortune, Feyre cannot forget Tamlin and cannot ignore that something terrible is unfolding in Prythian. Learning the truth of the curse - that a cruel queen named Amarantha rules Under the Mountain, holds the High Lords in thrall, and has now taken Tamlin - Feyre resolves to return and save him, even knowing it may cost her life. She crosses back into the faerie lands and makes her way Under the Mountain, into Amarantha's court, offering herself in exchange for a chance to free Tamlin and his people.

Under the Mountain, Amarantha sets Feyre a bargain: complete three deadly trials, or solve a riddle, to win Tamlin's freedom and break her hold on the courts. Feyre survives the first trial, a fight against an enormous burrowing monster, with hidden help. Rhysand offers his aid in her worst moments, but at a price - a magical bargain that binds Feyre to spend one week of every month in his Night Court thereafter, and forces her to play a humiliating public role at his side. Battered, drugged, and displayed for Amarantha's cruel amusement, Feyre endures the second trial and clings to her resolve as the final test approaches.

In the last trial Feyre must stab three hooded faeries through the heart. Two are innocents she is forced to kill; the third is Tamlin, whose heart Amarantha has secretly turned to stone so the blade cannot harm him. Even after Feyre passes, Amarantha refuses to free the courts because the riddle was never solved. Feyre speaks the answer aloud - love - and Amarantha, in a fury, kills her. The seven High Lords each give a portion of their power to resurrect Feyre as an immortal High Fae. Freed at last, Tamlin destroys Amarantha, lifting the curse and the blight from Prythian. Feyre returns to the Spring Court remade and reunited with Tamlin, but scarred by the deaths she caused and bound by the bargain that still ties her to Rhysand and the Night Court.

characters.description: The narrator, an immortal High Fae and the High Lady of the Night Court, and Rhysand's mate. As the book opens she is back at the Spring Court, playing the part of Tamlin's recovered bride while secretly working as a spy and saboteur, feeding intelligence to the Night Court and quietly turning Tamlin's people against him as war with Hybern nears.
characters.name: Feyre Archeron

characters.description: The High Lord of the Night Court, Feyre's mate and her equal as High Lord and Lady. Powerful, cunning, and devoted to his people and his inner circle, he leads the effort to unite Prythian against the King of Hybern.
characters.name: Rhysand

characters.description: The High Lord of the Spring Court, once Feyre's rescuer and betrothed, who allied with Hybern in a desperate bid to reclaim her. Believing Feyre has returned to him, he does not know she is now his enemy, working to unravel his court from within.
characters.name: Tamlin

characters.description: A red-haired Spring Court faerie with a mechanical golden eye, Tamlin's friend and emissary. Torn between old loyalties and his conscience, he is bound by the revelation that Feyre's newly made sister Elain is his mate.
characters.name: Lucien

characters.description: Feyre's proud, sharp-tongued eldest sister, forced into the Cauldron and remade as a High Fae against her will. Furious at the transformation and at the faerie world, she carries something powerful and unsettling taken from the Cauldron itself.
characters.name: Nesta Archeron

characters.description: Feyre's gentle middle sister, also thrown into the Cauldron and made High Fae. Shattered by the change and by the loss of her human betrothal, she is quiet and withdrawn as she struggles to adjust to what she has become.
characters.name: Elain Archeron

characters.description: Rhysand's cousin and a member of his inner circle, warm, bold, and fiercely loyal. Third in command of the Night Court, she is one of Feyre's closest friends and a key figure in the war effort.
characters.name: Morrigan

characters.description: A winged Illyrian warrior who commands the Night Court's armies, brash, battle-hardened, and quick to laughter. Devoted to Rhysand's inner circle, he prepares the Illyrian legions for the coming war and is drawn to Feyre's sister Nesta.
characters.name: Cassian

characters.description: A quiet, shadowed Illyrian warrior and the Night Court's spymaster, winged and marked by a painful past. Reserved and intensely loyal, he gathers intelligence for Rhysand and grows protective of Elain.
characters.name: Azriel

characters.description: Rhysand's second in command, an ancient and dangerous being wearing the small body of a High Fae woman with silver eyes. Older than the courts, she alone can wield the power needed to face the Cauldron directly.
characters.name: Amren

characters.description: The ancient, ruthless ruler of Hybern who wields the Cauldron and means to tear down the wall, conquer the human lands, and crush the faerie courts. His invasion is the war the whole book turns on.
characters.name: The King of Hybern

recaps.ending: The final battle against Hybern's forces turns on desperate sacrifice. Rhysand pours out his life to fuse the power of the High Lords in a spell that can turn the tide, and he dies. Feyre, refusing to lose him, appeals to the gathered High Lords to give a portion of their own power to bring him back, just as they once resurrected her Under the Mountain; they do, and Rhysand lives again. The King of Hybern is killed and his army shattered, ending the invasion. The cost is heavy - lives lost, courts wounded, old wrongs left to heal - but Prythian is free. Feyre and Rhysand stand together as High Lord and Lady of a restored Night Court, their inner circle intact. Nesta and Elain remain changed and still finding their place in the faerie world, and the human lands and faerie courts face an uneasy new peace. The immediate war is won, and the survivors turn toward rebuilding the world they nearly lost.
recaps.in_short: Feyre is entrenched in the Spring Court as a spy, quietly wrecking Tamlin's alliance with Hybern and turning his people against him before escaping back to the Night Court with Lucien. With the King of Hybern's invasion looming, Feyre and Rhysand work to unite Prythian's fractious High Lords, gather armies, and counter the Cauldron. Feyre's remade sisters struggle with their new Fae natures: Nesta carries a terrible power taken from the Cauldron, and Elain begins to see visions. The war brings brutal battles, shifting alliances, betrayals, and heavy losses, and Elain is captured by Hybern before being rescued. In the climactic battle Rhysand sacrifices himself to bind the courts' power together and dies, and Feyre persuades the assembled High Lords to resurrect him as they once resurrected her. The King of Hybern is killed, his forces broken. Prythian survives at great cost, the Night Court's family is whole again, and a fragile peace settles over the courts as they begin to rebuild.

recaps.text: Previously: mortal huntress Feyre Archeron was taken into the faerie realm of Prythian, fell in love with Tamlin of the Spring Court, and freed the High Lords from the tyrant Amarantha Under the Mountain, dying and being resurrected as an immortal High Fae. Stifled afterward by Tamlin's smothering protection, she was drawn to the Night Court and its High Lord, Rhysand, discovering he had hidden his true, honorable self behind a cruel mask. Feyre learned she and Rhysand are mates, became the High Lady of the Night Court, and joined his inner circle to fight the King of Hybern, who means to use the ancient Cauldron to conquer both realms. In the struggle, Feyre's mortal sisters Nesta and Elain were forced into the Cauldron and remade as High Fae, and Tamlin allied with Hybern to win Feyre back. To fight the enemy from within, Feyre let Tamlin take her to the Spring Court while secretly serving as a spy for the Night Court, hiding her true allegiance.

At the Spring Court, Feyre plays the recovered bride while methodically sabotaging Tamlin from within, sowing distrust among his allies and undermining his pact with Hybern. When her cover has done its work and grows too dangerous, she escapes back to the Night Court, taking Lucien with her. Reunited with Rhysand and his inner circle, Feyre turns to the enormous task ahead: the King of Hybern's invasion is coming, the Cauldron gives him terrifying power, and the divided High Lords of Prythian have never united against a common enemy.

The Night Court races to prepare for war, marshaling the Illyrian legions and seeking alliances among the other courts, including a fraught gathering of the High Lords who have never trusted one another. Feyre's remade sisters strain against their new natures: Nesta is volatile and carries a strange, immense power drawn from the Cauldron, while Elain grows quiet and begins to glimpse things that have not yet happened. The group works to understand the Cauldron and the ancient book that might counter it, even as Hybern's forces begin to move and the first blows of the war fall.

The war erupts in full. Battles test the alliance and its armies, and betrayals and hard bargains complicate the courts' fragile unity. Hybern strikes at the people Feyre loves, and Elain is seized by the enemy before being rescued in a daring effort. Amren prepares to wield the power that might turn the Cauldron against Hybern, at great personal risk. As losses mount and the enemy's strength becomes clear, Feyre, Rhysand, and their allies gather everything they have for a final confrontation they may not survive.

In the climactic battle, Rhysand sacrifices his life to bind the High Lords' power into a spell that can break Hybern, and he dies. Feyre refuses to accept it and persuades the assembled High Lords to give up a share of their own power to resurrect him, as they once resurrected her; Rhysand returns to life. The King of Hybern is killed and his army destroyed, ending the invasion. Prythian survives, though at a terrible price in lives and wounds. Feyre and Rhysand stand together over a restored Night Court with their family intact, Nesta and Elain still adjusting to their changed lives, and the courts and human lands settling into an uneasy peace as everyone begins the work of rebuilding.
